does: Steeps just-fried food in a sharp, sweet sauce while it is still hot, so that it drinks up the sauce and turns juicy and flavoured through.

intro.what: This method steeps freshly fried food in a sharp sweet sauce while it is hot.
intro.why: It teaches you to use absorption to flavour a crust while controlling how far that crust softens.

how: Make the sauce ahead and have it in a shallow dish.
Fry the food and lift it out of the oil, shaking off the excess.
Put the hot food straight into the sauce and turn it once.
Leave it to steep for a while, turning it now and then, then lift out and serve.

cues.text: The sharp, sweet scent of the sauce rises as the hot food goes in.
The crust has softened slightly and the food is juicy.

mistakes.mistake: Putting the food into the sauce after it has cooled, so that it will not take it up.
mistakes.fix: Put it in hot, as it comes from the oil.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving it in the sauce for too long, so that it turns mushy.
mistakes.fix: Lift it out after a short while.

quiz.question: What does the sauce soak contribute to fried food?
choices: A drier crust with no sauce absorbed.
A coating that must stay entirely separate.
quiz.because: Steeping lets sauce enter the hot food rather than remaining only on its surface.

quiz.question: When should fried food meet the prepared sauce?
choices: While still hot after excess oil is shaken off.
Only after cooling completely on a tray.
While still carrying a pool of frying oil.
quiz.because: Add the food hot for this absorption method, after shaking off excess frying oil so it does not enter the sauce.

quiz.question: Which texture is the aim after a brief steep?
choices: A fully dissolved crust and collapsed pieces.
A slightly softened crust with juicy food beneath.
A dry interior unchanged by the sauce.
quiz.because: Some softening is intended, but the food should retain its structure.

quiz.question: The fried pieces became mushy. What would you change next time?
choices: Cover them with more sauce and wait.
quiz.because: A shorter steep limits the amount of structural softening while retaining sauce flavour.

variant_of.differs: Hot, fried food is steeped in a seasoned sauce, not left in water, and the soak lasts only as long as the food needs to drink the sauce.
